skills.principle: When an authoritative correction replaces an input used by a prior conclusion, invalidate that conclusion and recompute every requested dependent result using the corrected input and the original valid rules.
procedure: Identify the original input, its authoritative replacement, and the prior conclusion marked as invalid.
Trace which parts of the requested result depend on the replaced input.
Retain assumptions, rates, offsets, and transformation rules that were not corrected or invalidated.
Recompute all affected outputs from the corrected input, propagating the change through each dependency.
Check that no superseded input or invalidated conclusion remains in the calculation.
Report the revised result clearly, including the corrected input and the key recomputation.
preconditions: An explicit correction supersedes a previously accepted input.
A prior conclusion was derived from that superseded input.
The requested output depends directly or indirectly on the corrected input.
The remaining calculation or scheduling rules are still valid and provide enough information to recompute the result.
counter_indications: Do not apply this procedure when the correction is unrelated to the requested output.
Do not alter conclusions that do not depend on the superseded input.
Do not reuse the invalidated conclusion merely because it was previously stored or stated.
Do not invent missing dependency rules, rates, offsets, or assumptions; request clarification when recomputation is underdetermined.

skills.principle: When a corrected source value supersedes an earlier value, invalidate every conclusion that depended on the earlier value and recompute it from the corrected value using the original dependency rules.
procedure: Identify the original source value, its corrected replacement, and the prior derived conclusion.
Treat the corrected value as authoritative and do not reuse the superseded value.
Determine how the prior conclusion was derived, including calculations, intervals, offsets, sequencing, and unchanged inputs.
Mark the dependent parts of the prior conclusion as invalid while preserving any parts that do not depend on the correction.
Recompute all affected outputs by applying the same derivation rules to the corrected value.
Check arithmetic, timing, units, ordering, and consistency with the corrected source.
preconditions: A source value has been explicitly corrected or superseded.
The requested conclusion depends directly or indirectly on that source value.
The derivation rule can be recovered from the prior reasoning or supplied context.
Other required inputs remain valid or have also been updated.
counter_indications: Do not apply this procedure when the alleged correction is merely an alternative, suggestion, or unconfirmed claim.
Do not alter conclusions that are independent of the corrected source value.
Do not preserve the original output merely because it was previously recorded as a decision.
Do not invent a derivation rule when the relationship between the source and requested output is unspecified or ambiguous; request clarification instead.

skills.principle: When a source fact is superseded, invalidate every conclusion that depends on it and recompute those conclusions from the corrected fact while preserving unaffected assumptions and rules.
procedure: Identify the original fact, its corrected replacement, and the conclusion marked as dependent on the original fact.
Treat the corrected fact as authoritative and stop using the superseded fact.
Determine the calculation, timing offset, dependency, or other transformation that produced the original conclusion.
Reapply that same transformation using the corrected fact, together with any still-valid assumptions.
Check all downstream conclusions for direct or indirect dependence and update each affected result.
Answer with the recalculated result and briefly indicate that it reflects the correction.
preconditions: A prior fact has been explicitly corrected or superseded.
The requested conclusion depends materially on the corrected fact.
The original derivation rule or dependency can be inferred or is provided.
Other inputs needed for recomputation remain valid or have also been updated.
counter_indications: Do not apply this procedure when the requested conclusion is independent of the corrected fact.
Do not retain or combine the superseded value with its replacement unless explicitly instructed.
Do not recompute when the correction is hypothetical, disputed, or later withdrawn.
Do not invent missing derivation rules, durations, quantities, or assumptions; request clarification when the updated result is underdetermined.

skills.principle: When an upstream fact is corrected, invalidate every conclusion that depended on it and recompute those conclusions from the corrected fact while preserving any unchanged timing, duration, or dependency rules.
procedure: Identify the original upstream fact, its corrected replacement, and the prior derived conclusion marked as invalid.
Determine the rule that linked the original fact to the derived conclusion, such as a lead-time offset, start-after dependency, fixed duration, or sequence of milestones.
Treat the corrected fact as authoritative and do not reuse the invalid conclusion as current information.
Apply the same unchanged dependency rule to the corrected fact to calculate the revised result.
Check that all dependent milestones were shifted or recalculated consistently and that the result satisfies the corrected constraints.
Answer the exact question with the revised values, optionally noting that the schedule or conclusion changed because of the correction.
preconditions: A prior conclusion was derived from an upstream fact that has since been explicitly corrected or superseded.
The dependency between the upstream fact and the requested result is stated or can be reliably inferred from the prior derivation.
The correction changes the input but does not itself replace the dependency rule used for recalculation.
counter_indications: Do not apply this procedure when the corrected fact is unrelated to the requested conclusion.
Do not preserve prior offsets or durations when the correction also changes scope, duration, sequencing, business-day rules, time zones, or other dependency constraints.
Do not invent a revised value when the dependency rule is ambiguous or insufficiently specified; request clarification instead.
Do not use the superseded fact or the invalidated conclusion as authoritative after an explicit correction.
